caveats: Here $n$ is the unweighted group count, $W$ is its total weight and $\hat p$ is the weighted group proportion; the first identity additionally uses the full observation count $N$.

These are audit reconstruction identities for the independent-respondent linearisation, not theorems printed in the letter; compatibility with rounded reported intervals does not independently identify the original analysis method.
Neither result establishes the inverse-variance assumptions for classical WLS standard errors, national survey-design validity, or 95% coverage.
No general inequality compares the unequal-weight survey variance with $\hat p(1-\hat p)/n$; the simple reduction in the first result requires equal weights.
The Lean results do not formalize the respondent-level reanalysis, validate the empirical percentages, or identify the effect of an information intervention.

key_results.what: For $N\ge2$ fixed binary responses and group indicators, positive weights and a nonempty group, weighted-ratio residuals sum to zero and their normalized squared sum equals $N/(N-1)$ times the squared-weight residual variance expression, whose inner expression reduces to $\hat p(1-\hat p)/n$ under equal weights.

For fixed binary responses and group indicators, positive weights and group count $n\ge2$, weighted residual sum of squares equals $W\hat p(1-\hat p)$, so the classical intercept-only WLS variance is $\hat p(1-\hat p)/(n-1)$.

overview.overview: This empirical letter reports weighted survey proportions relating gun-law knowledge, policy preferences and political engagement. Its Lean development is limited to two finite algebraic reconstructions: the residual and normalization identities for a weighted-ratio variance calculation, and the classical intercept-only weighted-least-squares variance formula. The letter prints no variance formula, and these results neither identify the historical procedure nor establish survey-design coverage or a causal effect of correcting misperceptions.

text.body: The proved statement takes $N\ge2$ fixed observations, binary group indicators $d_i$ and answers $y_i$, positive weights $w_i$, and $n=\sum_i d_i>0$. Put $W=\sum_i d_iw_i$, $\hat p=\sum_i d_iw_iy_i/W$ and $z_i=d_iw_i(y_i-\hat p)$. It asserts $\sum_i z_i=0$ and $\frac{\sum_i z_i^2/[N(N-1)]}{(W/N)^2} =\frac{N}{N-1}\frac{\sum_i d_iw_i^2(y_i-\hat p)^2}{W^2}.$ If all weights equal a positive constant, the inner ratio on the right equals $\hat p(1-\hat p)/n$. Positivity of $W$ is derived from the stated conditions. These are finite identities used by the conditional reconstruction. They neither identify the original procedure nor establish national survey coverage.
text.headline: Conditional weighted-ratio reconstruction identities
text.location: The independent-respondent linearisation in the evidence for P054-N001; the letter prints no variance formula

text.body: With the preceding fixed binary data and positive weights, now require $n\ge2$. The proved statement gives $\sum_i d_iw_i(y_i-\hat p)^2=W\hat p(1-\hat p),\qquad \frac{\sum_i d_iw_i(y_i-\hat p)^2}{(n-1)W} =\frac{\hat p(1-\hat p)}{n-1} =\frac{n}{n-1}\frac{\hat p(1-\hat p)}n.$ The displayed variance uses the classical intercept-only formula. Its algebra establishes neither the inverse-variance assumptions that justify classical standard errors nor the historical use of that procedure. No general comparison of the unequal-weight survey variance with the unweighted formula is asserted.
text.headline: Conditional classical intercept-only weighted-least-squares identity
text.location: The classical-WLS reconstruction in the evidence for P054-N001; the letter prints no variance formula
